_source: AI-researched venue CANDIDATES for Manchester and Cheshire, awaiting review — never directly edited by the research agent. Populated by a daily scheduled research agent (2026-08, at explicit user request: 'fan out some research agents who's goal is to run every day to find and suggest new businesses... they shouldn't go beyond cheshire and manchester just yet'; bumped from ~3-5/day to 10/day at a later explicit request). See .claude/agents/curia-research-daily.md for the full research brief/rules this agent works under (Hard rule 1 chain/fast-food screening, real coordinates only, no duplicates, Do/Drink/Eat coverage balance). The research agent commits straight to master for this file (no PR — this queue has zero effect on the live app, nothing reads it except the review agent and the admin dashboard's Growth Insights context). A second, independent daily agent (.claude/agents/curia-suggestion-review.md) re-verifies each `pending` entry and is the thing that promotes one into the real docs/data/venues.json, pushing straight to master after its own independent re-verification (see that file's own 2026-09-04 doc comment for why the human checkpoint moved to Curia Command's Pending Review tab instead of a PR here). Each entry mirrors docs/data/venues.json's own raw shape (name/district/type/spend/lat/lon/base/bands/reason) exactly, so a reviewed-and-approved entry can be moved into that file with a straight copy-paste, plus review-only fields (suggestedDate, status, researchNotes) that get stripped on promotion. `district` values must be a real existing district id from docs/data/districts.json (manchester/cheshire metros only) UNLESS the entry is itself proposing a brand-new district — see district-suggestions.json for that case instead; a venue suggestion should never invent a district id that doesn't exist anywhere.
_reviewWorkflow: status starts 'pending' on every new entry. The daily curia-suggestion-review agent changes it to 'approved'/promoted (then copies the venue fields into docs/data/venues.json and removes the entry here, pushed straight to master) or 'rejected' (left here with researchNotes explaining why, as a record so the same candidate isn't re-suggested later — curia-research-daily checks every entry here regardless of status before suggesting anything new). Genuinely uncertain candidates go to docs/data/pending-review-queue.json instead, staying 'pending' here until a human decides via Curia Command. A human's actual review happens by reading Curia Command's daily briefing and Pending Review tab, not by editing this file directly, though a human reviewer (or a future admin-dashboard screen) can still hand-edit an entry's status here if needed.

suggestions.name: Clark Art
suggestions.reason: Bill Clark's own gallery on Ashley Road since 1999, deep in L.S. Lowry and the northern painters he's written the books on — a private dealer's eye, not a gallery chain's algorithm.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Clark Art (155 Ashley Road, Hale) closed permanently on 3 October 2024 after 18 years, per Bill Clark's own retirement announcement (reported by Altrincham Today, 'An incredible journey: Clark Art to close after 18 years in Hale village'). The prior research pass's sources (Tripadvisor/Artsy/halebarns.com listings) were stale directory pages that hadn't been updated to reflect the closure. Do not re-suggest — the gallery no longer exists.

suggestions.name: Yang Sing
suggestions.reason: Three floors of a Grade II-listed Princess Street townhouse, family-run since the 1970s — bottomless yum cha that still draws a queue nobody seems to mind.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Yang Sing (34 Princess Street) has been closed since December 2021/early 2022 (kitchen fire, then a lease dispute) and Yang Sing Limited is now in liquidation per Companies House — it never reopened despite the owner's 2022 hope to reopen by 2023/24. The prior research pass's sources (visitmanchester.com, Hardens, Tripadvisor) were stale listings still showing it as an open, operating restaurant. Do not re-suggest unless it demonstrably reopens under new ownership.

suggestions.name: Blue Lobster
suggestions.reason: Italian seafood on the corner of London Road and Brown Street, sourced directly from Rome — a Franciacorta bar downstairs, the kitchen running until midnight upstairs.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Blue Lobster (34 London Road, Alderley Edge) closed permanently in December 2017, less than nine months after its April 2017 opening, following a staff-payment dispute with owner Andrea Zecchino (reported by alderleyedge.com and Manchester Confidential at the time). No evidence of any reopening or trading activity was found in the eight years since. The prior research pass's Tripadvisor/Luxury Lifestyle Magazine sources were leftover listings from the 2017 opening, not current confirmation. Do not re-suggest unless it demonstrably reopens under new ownership.

suggestions.name: Fire Station Social Cucina
suggestions.reason: A pizza theatre and wood oven where Gusto used to sit on London Road — hand-rolled pasta, Napoli-style bases, and only one other room anywhere doing the same thing.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via thebusinessdesk.com, wilmslow.co.uk/alderleyedge.com and the operator's own site (firestationsocial.co.uk): Fire Station Social Cucina, 75 London Road, Alderley Edge SK9 7DY, opened 10 June 2026 in the former Gusto unit — the second site for this specific concept, after the original in Tarporley. Run by 'Project Social Cucina', the restaurant division of Cheshire Pub Company (a separate entity from the 7-pub Cheshire Cat group already referenced elsewhere in this file) — only 2 sites confirmed under the Fire Station Social Cucina name itself, the same 2-site sibling precedent already used for Cibo/Suburban Green/Smoke Wilmslow/Heddy's/Caramello. Flagged for the reviewer: the parent company's own press describes this as 'expansion', so worth a quick re-check at promotion time that a third site hasn't since appeared. Moderate-high confidence otherwise — real, recently opened, well-covered locally, no closure signals. Re-checked again 2026-09-08 (curia-suggestion-review daily pass) specifically for a rumoured third site: none found — same 2-site status as this note originally recorded, still pending, still in docs/data/pending-review-queue.json for a human call rather than re-decided here. DECIDED 2026-09-08 by direct user instruction, in an interactive session: promoted into venues.json with the new `status: 'coming-soon'` field (added the same day specifically for this case) rather than a flat yes/no — real venue, passes Hard rule 1 on site count today, but its editorial confidence marker stays provisional given the parent's stated expansion plans. See venues.json's own note on the new field.

suggestions.name: The Copper Room
suggestions.reason: Amy and Rick Armstrong crowdfunded their way into Charles Roe House's Grade II* rooms — steak and seafood cooked properly, in a silk merchant's own dining room on Chestergate.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via the operator's own site (chefrick.co.uk), Macclesfield Nub News (two separate pieces confirming both the Kickstarter-funded opening and the venue name) and Tripadvisor (active listing with 2026-dated reviews): The Copper Room, Charles Roe House, 60-62 Chestergate, Macclesfield SK11 6DY, a fine-dining restaurant and cocktail bar run by chef-owners Amy and Rick Armstrong. No second site or group ownership found anywhere — single-site, independently owned, passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Coordinates from doogal.co.uk's postcode geocode for SK11 6DY. Reuses the existing FINE DINING type. Fills a real gap: Macclesfield had only 1 Eat-category venue (Chestergate Bistro) against 2 Do and 3 Drink before this addition. REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-14: the chef-owned fine-dining concept this candidate described no longer trades at 60-62 Chestergate. Charles Roe House's dining room changed to 'Piccante at The Copper Room' (Italian/Brazilian tapas, opened Dec 2022) and per Macclesfield Nub News that room has sat empty since summer 2025 while the building is converted into a different, unrelated venture, 'The Charles Roe Pub' (reopening Dec 2025). Amy and Rick Armstrong's ownership story checks out, but whatever they run today is not trading at this address under this description — a closure/identity mismatch, not a chain issue. Do not re-suggest at this address; a genuinely reopened Armstrong-run venue elsewhere would need its own fresh verification.

suggestions.name: Prana
suggestions.reason: Two floors of proper acoustics on Ashley Road from the team behind Stockport's Amp — order the cocktail, but the stage is the reason to stay past nine.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via CAMRA (camra.org.uk), whatpub.com and Altrincham Today: Prana, 14-16 Ashley Road, Altrincham WA14 2DW, an independent live-music venue and cocktail bar opened November 2023, run by the same team as Amp in Stockport — a real 2-site sibling pair, not a chain, same precedent as Bramhall/Cheadle Hulme's Mounting Stone/Chiverton Tap pair in this batch. RE-VERIFICATION 2026-09-11 (curia-suggestion-review) found the original researcher's 'CAMRA-listed and actively promoted' claim was incomplete: CAMRA and whatpub.com both actually list Prana as 'Closed Long Term' (last updated 28/05/2024), following a reported 'closing until further notice' Facebook announcement from Altrincham Today around the same date — a real closure signal the original pass missed. However, a new company, PRANA F&B LIMITED, was incorporated 13 September 2024 at the same 14-16 Ashley Road address and remains active per Companies House, and a Food Hygiene Ratings record exists for 'Prana - Altrincham' — both consistent with a reopening or change of hands rather than the site sitting empty, but no direct evidence of current 2025/2026 trading (a recent event listing, an active social post) was found either way. Genuinely conflicting signals rather than a clean pass or fail — left pending here and sent to docs/data/pending-review-queue.json for a human call rather than promoted or rejected outright. RE-CHECKED 2026-09-12 (curia-suggestion-review): Curia Command's pending_review collection had no decision recorded yet; still no direct 2026 trading evidence found either way. Left as-is. RE-CHECKED 2026-09-13 (curia-suggestion-review): still no direct 2025/2026 trading evidence either way despite fresh searches (Instagram/Skiddle listings exist for the venue but show no current events; two of this run's source URLs, altrincham.co.uk's own listing and a Skiddle venue page, were blocked by this session's network egress policy and couldn't be checked directly). One new detail surfaced: a Facebook report from around the 2024 closure mentions the owner's intent to convert the venue into an events space, which doesn't resolve whether it's trading today. Curia Command's pending_review collection was empty again this run — no human decision yet. This file previously carried an accidental duplicate of this exact entry (identical content, same 2026-09-11 suggestedDate) — deduplicated down to one today; no information was lost, the surviving entry already carried the fuller, more recently updated research notes. Left pending, unchanged in verdict, same as every prior run since 2026-09-11. RE-CHECKED 2026-09-14 (curia-suggestion-review): fresh search specifically for anything dated 2026 or late 2025 (recent reviews, active social media, current event listings, local news) found nothing new confirming current trading, and nothing new confirming a permanent closure/re-let either — the CAMRA/whatpub 'Closed Long Term' record and the active PRANA F&B LIMITED company/food hygiene registration both stand unchanged. Curia Command's pending_review collection was checked and had no decision recorded yet. Genuinely unresolved, unchanged in verdict since 2026-09-11. RE-CHECKED 2026-09-15 (curia-suggestion-review): Curia Command's pending_review collection still empty, no decision recorded. No new search performed this run beyond the standing checks — unchanged since 2026-09-11, still sitting in docs/data/pending-review-queue.json for a human call. RE-CHECKED 2026-09-17 (curia-suggestion-review): no re-check was actually possible this run — a genuine research-tool outage (WebSearch returning 'unavailable' on most queries or surfacing only Wikipedia noise; WebFetch EGRESS_BLOCKED for Google/Bing/DuckDuckGo/Instagram/Facebook/Tripadvisor/Companies House/CAMRA/whatpub/even plain Wikipedia) meant no new evidence could be found either way. This is a tooling gap, not a fresh 'still unresolved' finding — left pending, unchanged, same status as every prior run. REJECTED 2026-09-18 (curia-suggestion-review), resolving the long-stuck pending-review-queue item the other way: fresh research this run found the unit itself, 14-16 Ashley Road, Altrincham WA14 2DW, is currently being marketed by two independent commercial property sources (LoopNet and commercial agent WT Gunson) as available 'fitted restaurant premises' — generic to-let/for-sale brochure language, not 'let to Prana'. A landlord/agent does not typically market a unit as available while a tenant is trading in it, and this is the first positive evidence (not just absence of evidence) pointing toward closed rather than open. CAMRA/whatpub still read 'Closed Long Term' (unchanged since 28/05/2024) and the Food Hygiene Rating's most recent inspection is still dated 24/05/2024, with no newer inspection, event listing, dated review or dated social post found despite many search angles across this and prior runs. PRANA F&B LIMITED remains 'active' on Companies House but with no trading evidence — treated as a dormant/live shell rather than an operating tenant. If PRANA F&B LIMITED actually relaunches the space, this should be re-researched from scratch, not assumed to inherit this rejection.

suggestions.name: Mouro Coffee Bar
suggestions.reason: Moroccan tile underfoot and a La Marzocco machine doing the actual work — focaccia sandwiches, matcha and affogato for a stretch of Heaton Moor Road that doesn't need to shout about any of it.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via Tripadvisor (5.0/5, current 2026 listing), the Food Standards Agency ratings register and the venue's own Instagram (@mourocoffeebar): Mouro Coffee Bar, 72 Heaton Moor Road, Stockport SK4 4NZ — a design-led independent coffee bar serving speciality coffee, cold-pressed juices, pastries and focaccia sandwiches. No second site or group ownership found anywhere despite a direct search; single-site, passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Coordinates from postcode geocode for SK4 4NZ. Reuses the existing BRUNCH SPOT type. Heaton Moor was at 8 venues (3 Do, 3 Drink, 2 Eat) before this addition — Eat was its thinnest category, and the district is one of ten currently under the 10-venue standing target. High confidence. REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-16: the 'no second site found anywhere' claim doesn't hold up — Mouro is in fact a real, actively expanding four-site coffee brand: the original Heaton Moor site, two Altrincham sites (25 Market Street and 8-10 Oxford Road, opened August 2025), and a fourth opened 16 May 2026 on Tib Street in the Northern Quarter itself (themanc.com's own coverage explicitly headlines it 'Mouro opens third coffee shop', undercounting even by its own count since two Altrincham sites exist). This is well past this file's established 2-3-site small-sibling-group allowance and spans two separate towns plus a city-centre expansion — a real, currently-growing chain by Hard rule 1's own standard, not a family pair. Do not re-suggest unless the brand's footprint materially contracts.

suggestions.name: Underbank
suggestions.reason: A former bank branch turned beer hall and soundsystem room at the crossroads of the two Underbanks — Pomona Island and Runaway on tap, and a rig loud enough that conversation moves to the beer garden after ten.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via CAMRA (camra.org.uk), manchesterwire.co.uk and themanc.com coverage of its 30-31 May 2025 grand opening: Underbank, 27 Great Underbank, Stockport SK1 1LN — a beer hall/soundsystem bar in a former RBS branch, opened by Des and Nina O'Malley (also behind Heaton Moor's Nook, a 2-site sibling pair within this file's existing small-group precedent). Explicitly confirmed as a distinct venue from the already-seeded 'The Underbank' (a separate bar/gig venue at a different address, founded by Benji Taylor) — same immediate street, different business, different owners; named 'Underbank' (no 'The') here to keep the two clearly distinguishable and avoid any implied duplicate. Coordinates approximated from the Great Underbank cluster of postcodes already used for neighbouring seeded venues (By Yon Orange, Sticky Fingers Bakery), since SK1 1LN itself didn't resolve to a precise lookup this session. Reuses the existing LIVE MUSIC BAR type (already used for MASH, Macclesfield) for a second venue. Stockport (Underbanks) was at 9 venues (3 Do, 3 Drink, 3 Eat) before this addition — one of ten districts currently under the 10-venue standing target. Moderate-high confidence (ownership/opening well-documented; exact coordinate is a close approximation). RE-VERIFICATION 2026-09-16 (curia-suggestion-review) found this candidate's own 'distinct from The Underbank' claim is more complicated than it reads: this file's already-promoted 'The Underbank' entry (2026-09-11) describes 'a former Cheshire bank... Pomona Island and Runaway on tap... the same husband-and-wife team behind Heaton Moor's Nook' — which is, fact for fact, the real venue actually branded 'Underbank' (no 'The'), i.e. this candidate's own subject, not a different business. A separate, third search independently confirms the real 'The Underbank' (with 'The') is instead Benji Taylor's live-music venue in the Syndikat building, which doesn't appear to have ever actually been seeded under that description. This reads as a naming/identity mix-up between two real, similarly-named venues on the same street — not a clean duplicate (the candidate and the existing entry aren't literally the same submission) and not a clean distinct-venue pass either. Sent to docs/data/pending-review-queue.json for a human call on how to resolve the mislabelling (rename the existing entry, add the Benji Taylor venue under the correct name, or something else); left 'pending' here rather than decided either way. RE-CHECKED 2026-09-17 (curia-suggestion-review): no re-check was actually possible this run — a genuine research-tool outage (WebSearch returning 'unavailable' on most queries or surfacing only Wikipedia noise; WebFetch EGRESS_BLOCKED for Google/Bing/DuckDuckGo/Instagram/Facebook/Tripadvisor/Companies House/CAMRA/whatpub/even plain Wikipedia) meant no new evidence could be found either way. This is a tooling gap, not a fresh 'still unresolved' finding — left pending, unchanged, same status as every prior run. RE-CHECKED 2026-09-18 (curia-suggestion-review): fresh research actually contradicts the working theory recorded above — the O'Malleys' venue's own channels (domain theunderbank.co.uk, its Instagram caption, its Facebook page name) all self-brand as 'The Underbank' (with 'The'), the opposite of the 'no The' framing assumed here; press/council sources more often drop the 'The' informally. No reliable evidence was found that Benji Taylor currently operates a second, separate venue under any 'Underbank' name — his documented 2024-2026 timeline has him stepping away from his own existing venue, Bask, on sick leave in 2024, Bask rebranding as an Irish pub ('Fitzpatrick's'), and Taylor returning specifically to Bask around April 2026, not to any Underbank-named venue. The two Stockport Nub News articles that originally seeded this mix-up theory could not be read directly this run (network-blocked, only search-engine summaries available), and Brook Underbank Ltd's (Companies House #14669490) officers list — which would settle who legally operates the venue — could not be retrieved either. Best-supported picture right now: there is likely only one venue at 27 Great Underbank, run by Des and Nina O'Malley, correctly already matching this file's existing 'The Underbank' entry, and no second venue needs adding. Left pending, no database change made — closing this out for good needs a direct read of the two Nub News articles, the Brook Underbank Ltd officers list, or a first-person check of Benji Taylor's own social accounts, none reachable this run.

suggestions.name: Olive Tree Brasserie
suggestions.reason: Meze and a bottomless brunch on Watergate Row since 2016 — Dean Wilson's third room, not his first draft, and it still runs on a Greek kitchen's own instincts.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via the venue's own site (olivetreebrasserie.co.uk), Tripadvisor (4.2/5, active 2026 reviews) and Facebook (92% recommend, 971 reviews): Olive Tree Brasserie, 39-41 Watergate Row, Chester CH1 2LE — Greek/Mediterranean brasserie, third site opened 2016 for Dean Wilson's small group (Lytham St Annes 2007, Preston 2012, Chester 2016). A genuine 3-town regional group, flagged accurately rather than claimed single-site — within the small-sibling-group allowance already established repeatedly elsewhere in this file (Wallop, The Creameries, Bar Six, all 3-site groups), not treated as a chain. One of several first venues for the newly-seeded Chester district. Coordinates from Watergate Street's own documented street coordinates, postcode-geocoding APIs being network-blocked this session. Reuses the existing GREEK TAVERNA type. Moderate confidence (3-site footprint is a real judgment call for the reviewer, though consistent with standing precedent). REVIEW ATTEMPTED 2026-09-17 (curia-suggestion-review): could not be independently re-verified this run due to a genuine research-tool outage — WebSearch returned 'unavailable' errors on most queries and otherwise surfaced only Wikipedia-indexed content (no Wikipedia coverage exists for this venue), and WebFetch was EGRESS_BLOCKED for every other domain tried (Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo, Instagram, Facebook, Tripadvisor, Companies House, CAMRA/whatpub). This is the highest-priority Chester candidate to re-check once tooling recovers — a claimed 3-site regional group (Lytham St Annes/Preston/Chester) is exactly the multi-region footprint Hard rule 1 exists to catch, and it was never independently confirmed beyond the original researcher's own notes. Left 'pending', unchanged, rather than promoted on trust or rejected without evidence. REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-18 (curia-suggestion-review): the operator, Dean Wilson, actually runs a currently-4-site group spanning three regions — Chester, Lytham (Bank House, replacing the original St Annes site which closed ~2018), Stockton Heath (Warrington, opened 2018) and Leeds (Pearl Chambers, opened December 2023, a genuine out-of-region expansion) — not the tidy 3-site Lancashire group (St Annes/Preston/Chester) the original candidate described; the Preston site also closed August 2021 after a landlord dispute, on top of St Annes closing earlier. This is well past this file's small-sibling-group allowance and reads as a real, currently-expanding regional chain. Separately, and independently disqualifying on its own: Dean Wilson was banned from acting as a company director for 10 years and 6 months (ruling reported November 2024) for exploiting the Covid-19 Bounce Back Loan scheme — two separate £50,000 loans taken against the one-loan-per-business rule, discovered during the Preston entity's insolvency. Sources: Blog Preston and Chester Standard coverage of the director ban, Leeds List's coverage of the Leeds opening, Blackpool Gazette on the St Annes/Lytham move, and the Lancashire Evening Post on the Preston closure. Do not re-suggest unless the group's footprint materially contracts back to a genuine small sibling pair.
